newsitem.title: USA: Ultramar-Diamond merger seen as defensive.
newsitem.headline: Ultramar-Diamond merger seen as defensive.

text.p: Ultramar Corp and Diamond Shamrock Inc are reinforcing their defenses against a possible takeover raid with their $850 million stock-swap merger agreement, according to arbitrageurs.
The arbs said they did not see any compelling strategic advantages to the combination, but the deal makes it less likely for either company to fall prey to a hostile buyer.
"I don't see many synergies, just the 200 or so corporate layoffs," one arb said.
"Ultramar especially has always been seen on the defensive with weak (earnings) numbers recently, so they may have done this to avoid a takeover," he said.
"It looks like Diamond Shamrock has been taken under (with an offer price below Friday's market close). I see very limited downside risk" to the deal, he added.
Ultramar and Diamond said the merger pact calls for conversion of each Diamond share into 1.02 shares of Ultramar.
Ultramar shares closed on Friday at 28-1/2 while Diamond closed at 30-1/4, both on the New York Stock Exchange.
Under the established ratio, Diamond Shamrock shares are valued at just over $29 each.
In early Monday trading, Diamond Shamrock fell two to 28-1/4 while Ultramar shed 3/8 to 28-1/8.
But the arbs said it was difficult to consider Diamond Shamrock "taken under" because the shares began a sharp ascent on September 12, when they stood at about $26.
In a stretch of unusually active trade that peaked September 18, the shares rose to neaqrly $32.
Diamond Shamrock is a refiner and marketer of petroleum products, primarily in the Southwest, and is a retailer of gasoline in Texas.
Ultramar is also a refiner, with most of its business based in Canada and California.
Last December Diamond Shamrock acquired National Convenience Stores for about $260 million, outbidding Circle K Corp.
Last spring, Circle K was acquired by Tosco Corp in a stock swap that valued Circle K at about $31.50 per share.
